ThreeSumSharpTail_Analysis:
For every real number $x$, define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$. Here and throughout these definitions, $\log$ is the total real logarithm: it is the natural logarithm on positive arguments, is $0$ at $0$, and equals $\log|x|$ on negative arguments. Thus $H$ is defined on all real numbers, not only $[0,1]$, and $H(0)=H(1)=0$.

For arbitrary real numbers $c$ and $\theta$, define $O(c,\theta)=\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$. No restriction on either argument is imposed.

For arbitrary real numbers $c$ and $\theta$, define $S(c,\theta)=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$. Real division is total, with division by $0$ equal to $0$, so this formula also defines $S(0,\theta)=-\theta\log9/\log4$.

For every real number $\theta$, define $Q(\theta)=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$; there is no interval restriction on $\theta$.

For every real number $c$, define $E(c)=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$ and division by zero is zero. In particular, $c=0$ is included and gives $E(0)=\log3/\log4$.

For all natural numbers $c,m,d$, including zero and without assuming $d\le m$ or $c\ge1$, define $B(c,m,d)=\binom{cm}{\max(m-d,0)}9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$. The subtractions inside the original natural-number expression are truncated at zero, and the exponent subtracts $m$ before adding $d$. The binomial coefficient is zero when its lower argument exceeds its upper argument. Consequently $B(c,0,d)=9^d$, and if $d>m$ the lower binomial argument is $0$, so $B(c,m,d)=9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$; these values are part of the definition even outside a tail range.
ThreeSumSharpTail.binomial_entropy_bound: For every pair of natural numbers $r,k$ satisfying $r\ge1$ and $0\le k\le r$, put $p=k/r$ as a real number and $H(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$, where $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm with its total real extension $\log0=0$ and $\log x=\log|x|$ for negative $x$. Then both inequalities $\exp(rH(p))/(r+1)\le\binom rk$ and $\binom rk\le\exp(rH(p))$ hold, with the binomial coefficient and natural parameters interpreted in the real numbers for these comparisons. Both endpoint cases $k=0$ and $k=r$ are included: $H(p)=0$ and the assertion is $1/(r+1)\le1\le1$. The case $r=0$ is excluded by the hypothesis.
ThreeSumSharpTail.sharp_normalized_tail: For every pair of natural numbers $c,m$ with $c>10$ and $m\ge1$, and every real $\theta$ with $0<\theta<9/10$, let $L=\lceil\theta m\rceil$; in this range the natural-number ceiling used in the statement is the ordinary ceiling and $1\le L\le m$. Define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, with the total real logarithm taking value $0$ at $0$ and the natural logarithm of the absolute value at a negative argument, and put $S=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$. Then $\displaystyle \frac{\sum_{d=L}^{m}\binom{cm}{m-d}9^{cm-m+d}}{\binom{cm}{m}9^{cm-m}}\le\frac{cm+1}{1-9/(c-1)}(4^m)^{-S}$. The sum includes both endpoints and is first formed as a natural number before being cast to the reals; every displayed division and the power with exponent $-S$ are real operations. The count used in the code is defined for arbitrary natural arguments by $\binom{cm}{\max(m-d,0)}9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$, but on the stated summation range no subtraction truncates. The denominator count and $1-9/(c-1)$ are strictly positive here. The cases $m=0$, $c\le10$, $\theta=0$, and $\theta=9/10$ are not asserted.
ThreeSumSharpTail.sharp_saving_strict: For every pair of real numbers $c,\theta$ satisfying $c>10$ and $0<\theta<9/10$, let $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm extended to be $0$ at zero and to equal the logarithm of the absolute value at negative arguments. Then both strict inequalities $0<\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$ and $\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4<[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$ hold. Here $c$ ranges over real numbers, not only integers; the arguments of the logarithms appearing after expansion of $H$ are positive under these hypotheses. None of the boundary values $c=10$, $\theta=0$, or $\theta=9/10$ is included.
ThreeSumSharpTail.admissible_parameters_: For every natural number $c$, real number $\theta$, and rational numbers $a,s,r$, assume $c>10$, $0<\theta<9/10$, $0<a<1$, and $0<s<1$. Define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, with the total real logarithm taking value $0$ at zero and the logarithm of the absolute value at negative arguments, $S=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, $Q=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, and $E=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$. Also assume the five strict real inequalities $a(E+S)<1$, $s<S$, $s<1/2-Q$, $\log7/\log2+3a/2<3-as/2$, and $2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2$, where natural and rational parameters are cast to the reals, together with the strict rational inequality $2-as/4<r$. The conclusion is the following quantified assertion about a specified machine: for every natural number $\kappa$, there exist a finite instruction list $P$, a natural number $b$, a function $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and a natural number $K$ such that $T(n)^q\le K n^{\max(p,0)}$ for every natural $n\ge2$, where $r=p/q$ is the reduced rational representation with integer numerator $p$ and positive natural denominator $q$. For every natural $n$, every integer sequence $(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ satisfying $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$ at every position, and every natural word width $W\ge b(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$, with the integer logarithm taken to be $0$ at $n=0$, running this same $P$ from instruction position $0$ halts within $T(n)$ steps with acceptance if and only if there exist three pairwise distinct positions $i,j,k$ in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with $x_i+x_j+x_k=0$ as integers. Memory consists of $W$-bit words at all integer addresses; initially address $0$ contains $n$ modulo $2^W$, addresses $1$ through $n$ contain the corresponding inputs modulo $2^W$, and every other address contains zero. An instruction may write the constant $1$ to a fixed integer address, add, subtract, or multiply words at two fixed addresses into another fixed address modulo $2^W$, load through an address read as a signed word, store through an address read as a signed word, jump to a specified natural instruction position if a fixed cell is negative when read as a signed word, accept, or reject. Indirect load writes into a fixed cell; indirect store reads its source from a fixed cell. Each instruction takes one step, writing proceeds to the next instruction, a non-taken conditional branch also proceeds to the next instruction, and executing beyond the finite list rejects. A halting instruction counts toward the time bound; with zero steps there is no verdict. There is no further condition on the final memory. The witnesses may depend on $\kappa$ and the initially fixed parameters but must work uniformly for every eligible $n$, input, and $W$, with no upper bound on $W$. The correctness requirement includes $n=0,1,2$, for which no three distinct positions exist and the verdict must be rejection; the polynomial inequality only constrains $n\ge2$. For $n=0$ the input magnitude condition is vacuous, and natural powers use $0^0=1$. The definition does not require $b>0$ or $K>0$, so if a chosen $b$ is zero the quantifier includes zero-width words. Under the parameter hypotheses $r>7/4$, so the numerator truncation in the time bound does not alter $p$. No claim is made for parameter choices failing any hypothesis, and no upper bound on $r$ is imposed.
ThreeSumSharpTail.explicit_parameter_cer: Let $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm extended by $\log0=0$ and by the logarithm of the absolute value on negative inputs. With the exact real constants $a=0.05665$, $s=0.06945$, and $t=0.11202$, define $S=[21H(1/21)-21H((1-t)/21)-t\log9]/\log4$, $Q=[H(t)+t\log9]/\log4$, and $E=[21\log10-21H(1/21)/2-20\log3]/\log4$. With no hypotheses or free parameters, the declaration asserts the conjunction of these seven statements: $a(E+S)<1$; $s<S$; $s<1/2-Q$; $\log7/\log2+3a/2<3-as/2$; $2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2$; the exact rational equality $2-0.05665\cdot0.06945/4=1.999016414375$; and the exact rational equality $1.999017-(2-0.05665\cdot0.06945/4)=0.000000585625$. The first five comparisons are strict comparisons of real numbers. The last two equalities are in the rational numbers, and every decimal in the statement denotes its exact terminating-decimal value, not a floating-point approximation. The declaration asserts these numerical statements and no machine-existence conclusion.
ThreeSumSharpTail.threeSum_1999017: For every natural number $\kappa$, there exist a finite instruction list $P$, a natural number $b$, a function $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and a natural number $K$ such that for every natural $n\ge2$, $T(n)^{1000000}\le K n^{1999017}$, and such that the following correctness condition holds. For every natural $n$, every integer sequence $(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ with $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$ at every position, and every natural word width $W\ge b(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$, taking the integer logarithm of $0$ to be $0$, the program $P$ started at instruction position $0$ halts within $T(n)$ steps and accepts if and only if three pairwise distinct positions $i,j,k\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfy $x_i+x_j+x_k=0$ as integers. Memory consists of $W$-bit words at every integer address. It initially contains $n$ modulo $2^W$ at address $0$, the input values in order modulo $2^W$ at addresses $1$ through $n$, and zero at every other address, including all negative addresses. The allowed instructions are: write constant $1$ to a fixed integer-addressed cell; add, subtract, or multiply two fixed cells into a fixed cell modulo $2^W$; load into a fixed cell from an address supplied by the signed interpretation of another fixed cell; store the value of a fixed cell at an address supplied by the signed interpretation of another fixed cell; jump to a fixed natural instruction position when a fixed cell has negative signed value; accept; and reject. Each instruction consumes one step. Writes and non-taken conditional jumps advance by one instruction, and a position beyond the list executes rejection. The halting instruction is counted, and zero available steps produce no verdict. The final memory has no output constraint. The same witnesses work for all eligible sizes, inputs, and word widths for the fixed $\kappa$; witnesses may vary with $\kappa$, and word width has no upper bound. Sizes $n=0,1,2$ are included in correctness and require rejection because three distinct positions do not exist, although the time inequality is imposed only for $n\ge2$. At $n=0$ the magnitude condition is vacuous, and natural exponentiation uses $0^0=1$. Neither $b$ nor $K$ is required to be positive, so a chosen $b=0$ would require correctness even at $W=0$. The exponent is the exact rational $1.999017=1999017/1000000$, which is why the time condition uses the displayed integer powers.
